format: x64 PE containing an RC4-encrypted PowerShell resource
recovery: Uppercase MD5 hex of a code-referenced eight-byte seed is the RC4 key. All addresses, key bytes and resource names come from the input.
behavior: Enumerates Win32_LogicalDisk, substitutes C:\Users for C:, and recursively selects files outside Windows paths.
Increments every byte modulo 256 in docx/txt/ps1/bat/vbs files and rewrites the original path.
Increments the first 11 bytes in pdf/avi/jpg/png/psd/mp4/mov/mp3/exe/msi files and rewrites the original path.
Downloads an image, sets HKCU Control Panel Desktop wallpaper, and refreshes desktop parameters.
Writes an embedded RSA public key to the desktop; the script never uses that key for encryption.
corrections: Retired native-folder-resource-file-encryptor: folder browsing, ordinary file APIs, resource entropy and a default manifest do not establish ransomware.
Moved placeholder-assembly-identity to metadata/binary/resource/identity; a default manifest is a property, not masquerading intent.
Recovered script findings describe destructive mutation and defacement without asserting cryptographic ransomware or extortion.
controls: check.py scans changed identifiers, changed destination/buffer, comments, standalone wallpaper configuration, and a single-file transform. The sibling cleave decoder tests changed seeds, image bases, section/resource names, benign scripts, malformed tables, missing markers and incorrect keys.
